name: Nintendo Switch family
summary: Explore Nintendo Switch family hardware and firmware-specific routes into homebrew across the original Erista, the Mariko revision, Lite and OLED.

specs.cpu: Custom NVIDIA Tegra X1: 4× Arm Cortex-A57 + 4× Cortex-A53 (Erista) or Mariko silicon (Mariko, Lite, OLED)
specs.storage: 32 GB eMMC (original, Mariko, Lite) or 64 GB eMMC (OLED); microSD card slot up to 2 TB
specs.video-out: HDMI up to 1080p via dock (not available on Lite)

variants.notes: HAC-001 motherboard with HAC-CPU-01/10/20 boards. Unpatched units accept the RCM payload on every firmware via a short between pins 10 and 11 of the X9 connector in recovery mode (fusee-gelee). Patched Erista units (same model code, different serial range) have the bug fixed and require a modchip.
HAC-001(-01) motherboard with HAD-CPU-10 board (Mariko silicon). The boot chain bug is patched; a modchip is required for any unofficial code.
HDH-001 motherboard with HDH-CPU-02 board. Handheld-only; no TV output, no detachable Joy-Con. Mariko silicon, patched boot chain. Modchip required.
HEG-001 motherboard with HEG-CPU-01 board. 7" OLED screen, wider kickstand, LAN port in dock. Mariko silicon, patched boot chain. Modchip required.

homebrew.name: Atmosphère
homebrew.firmware: One firmware line per release; 1.12.1 targets services introduced in firmware 23.0.0
homebrew.summary: Custom firmware for the Switch. It replaces the stock kernel (exosphere), provides a homebrew launcher (hbl/hbmenu), and includes fs/dns MITM capabilities. Update CFW and firmware together — never firmware alone.

compatibility.note: Atmosphère's README describes a custom Switch firmware replacing the stock kernel with exosphere. It targets any console able to load fusee; project compatibility requires an exploit or modchip for patched models. Firmware release line is 1.12.1 for 23.0.0.

requirements: An exploitable entry point: fusee-gelee via RCM on unpatched Erista, or a modchip on patched Erista / Mariko / Lite / OLED.
Atmosphere payload loaded through hekate (or modchip firmware) before first boot.
warnings: Updating system firmware without updating Atmosphère first can leave the console unable to boot CFW until a matching release ships.

homebrew.name: hekate
homebrew.firmware: Every firmware; it is a bootloader, not an exploit
homebrew.summary: Bootloader, partition manager and backup tool. Boots Atmosphère (sysNAND or emuMMC), stock firmware, Android and Linux, and manages SD/eMMC partitions. It does not provide the exploit — it runs after one.

compatibility.note: hekate runs on every Switch model and firmware; it does not bypass the signed boot chain on its own. A payload must be delivered via RCM (unpatched Erista) or a modchip to launch hekate first.

requirements: An exploit payload (fusee-gelee via RCM or modchip) to boot hekate initially.
At least one NAND backup (with hekate) before first CFW write.
warnings: A corrupted boot0/boot1 requires hardware-level recovery; there is no consumer unbrick tool.

homebrew.name: fusee-gelee (RCM payload)
homebrew.firmware: Every firmware; closed on all patched models
homebrew.summary: A payload that exploits a boot-ROM bug (recovery mode) to load unsigned code over USB. It works on unpatched Erista consoles on every firmware version. All other Switch models have the bug fixed.

compatibility.note: Upstream and the record summary: works on unpatched Erista consoles on every firmware version.
The boot-ROM bug is fixed on these models; they need a modchip instead.

requirements: An unpatched Erista Switch (HAC-001 with early board revision).
A way to enter RCM (jig or grounded pin on X9 connector pins 10–11).
A PC or phone running a payload sender (e.g. TegraRcmGUI).
warnings: Patched Erista, Mariko, Lite and OLED consoles have the RCM bug fixed; no software route exists without a modchip.

homebrew.name: Spacecraft-NX (modchip firmware)
homebrew.summary: Open-source firmware for SX Core/Lite-compatible hardware glitch chips. Glitches the boot chain at power-on to run a payload. Does not boot Horizon on its own and cannot pirate games.

compatibility.note: Modchip firmware glitches the boot chain before Horizon loads, so it is not tied to a system version.
Unpatched Erista consoles use the RCM route instead; a modchip is not required.

requirements: A modchip soldered to the Switch motherboard.
A PC connected via USB to flash the chip firmware.
warnings: A bad modchip install or corrupted boot0/boot1 requires hardware-level recovery.

homebrew.name: switchroot Linux 4 Switch
homebrew.firmware: Depends on bootloader; not a standalone firmware path
homebrew.summary: Ubuntu and Fedora Linux images for the Switch, installed to SD or eMMC and booted through hekate. The wiki lists Ubuntu 18.04, 22.04, 24.04 and Fedora 39/41/42 with separate install guides.

compatibility.note: Linux replaces the boot target, not the exploit. hekate must still be launched from RCM or modchip first. The wiki lists images for all Switch models.

requirements: hekate already running on the console.
A microSD card with sufficient space for the Linux image.
warnings: Partitioning the SD card for Linux erases it.

homebrew.name: switchroot Android
homebrew.firmware: Depends on bootloader; not a standalone firmware path
homebrew.summary: LineageOS-based Android builds for the Switch. The current build targets all models; an older Android 10 build was v1-only.

compatibility.note: Current build claims all Switch models. Android 10 was documented for v1 (unpatched Erista) only. Read the model line on the download page before flashing.

requirements: hekate already running on the console.
A microSD card with sufficient space for the Android image.
warnings: Partitioning the SD card for Android erases it.

homebrew.name: Homebrew App Store
homebrew.firmware: Runs from the Homebrew Menu under Atmosphère; no firmware matrix is published.
homebrew.summary: A GUI store for open-source Switch homebrew, with browsing, downloads and updates from the console.

compatibility.note: README: place it in sd:/switch/appstore and run it from hbmenu; the console needs homebrew access.

requirements: A Switch running Atmosphère with the Homebrew Menu.
An SD card for the app and its downloads.
warnings: Only lists open-source homebrew; review each app before installing it.
homebrew.availability: Open source (GPL-3.0); releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: nx-hbmenu (Homebrew Menu)
homebrew.firmware: Loaded by Atmosphère once an entry point runs; no firmware matrix is published.
homebrew.summary: The Homebrew Menu for Switch. It lists and launches homebrew from the SD card and is included with Atmosphère.

compatibility.note: README documents the SD layout and release; it is the menu Atmosphère loads after an entry point.

requirements: A Switch that can run Atmosphère.
An SD card with homebrew in the documented layout.
warnings: The menu only launches homebrew; it does not provide the entry point itself.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: TegraExplorer
homebrew.firmware: Payload injection needs an unpatched Erista console or a modchip; the project does not list console firmware versions.
homebrew.summary: A payload-based file explorer for Switch. It browses and edits SD and NAND contents and runs scripts before Horizon starts.

compatibility.note: README: inject TegraExplorer as a payload; unpatched Erista consoles accept RCM payloads on any firmware.
These models need a modchip to run payloads; the project does not list modchip models.

requirements: An unpatched Erista console with a payload injector, or a modchip on a patched console.
An SD card for the files you want to browse or edit.
warnings: Writing to NAND can brick the console; the project warns to keep backups.
No entry point is provided by the app itself.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: MissionControl
homebrew.firmware: The project says it supports all Switch firmware versions; it requires Atmosphère.
homebrew.summary: A sysmodule that connects controllers from other consoles over Bluetooth, with rumble, motion and native pairing menus.

compatibility.note: README: supports all Switch firmware versions; install requires Atmosphère.

requirements: A Switch running Atmosphère.
An SD card for the sysmodule files.
warnings: Controller compatibility varies by model; see the project compatibility list.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: Checkpoint
homebrew.firmware: Homebrew app; needs Atmosphère and the Homebrew Menu.
homebrew.summary: A save manager for Switch and 3DS. It backs up and restores saves for the titles you have played.

compatibility.note: README describes a homebrew save manager for Switch; it runs under an existing homebrew environment.

requirements: A Switch running Atmosphère with the Homebrew Menu.
An SD card for the backup files.
warnings: Restoring a save overwrites the current save; keep the original backup.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.
